In summary, our research is concerned with
a better understanding of the microscopic description of BPS black holes in string theory, and in particular with the study of their microscopic origin as bound states of branes.
the construction of a new class of BPS black holes in string theory, which are characterized by a nontrivial axionic background.

the study of the generating solution of BPS black holes, which is a solution of the supergravity equations of motion with the property that all other supersymmetric black hole solutions are obtained by a U–duality transformation from this solution.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
all the BPS black holes of toroidally–compactified type IIB and M theory are made of D–brane bound states and that their microscopic and macroscopic descriptions are equivalent.

the 56–dimension U–duality group is completely broken by the black hole solution and that the microscopic description of the black hole solution is given by the bound state of 56 D–branes with a non–trivial angle among them.

the U–duality invariant BPS black holes of toroidally–compactified type IIA and IIB string theories are bound states of D–brane and anti–D–brane configurations, with the number of D–brane and anti–Dbrane constituents equal to the rank of the corresponding gauge group.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the U–duality group acts on the axions in a way that is consistent with the known action of U–duality on the D–brane charges.
the BPS black holes in toroidally compactifed string (and M)-theory are described by a bound state of D–brane and anti–D–brane.
we have constructed the generating solution for the BPS black holes, giving both the macroscopic (supergravity) and microscopic (bound state of D–brane) description of it.
The main takeaway from our work is that
all the 56–dimension U–duality orbits of BPS black holes are generated from the same solution by means of a simple change of U–duality frame.
the BPS black holes in toroidally compactfied string (and M–) theory can be described in a very natural way by a bound state of D–brane.

, for the BPS black holes, the microscopic description in terms of D–brane bound states can be obtained directly from the macroscopic one in terms of supergravity fields, without having to go through a full U–duality transformation.
